fact: EMIS describes the STI as account-to-account interoperability between bank and non-bank payment service providers, and KWiK processed 4.48 million transfers worth Kz 123.85 billion in August 2026.

Expansão reports EMIS data that digital wallets originated Kz 212.7bn of the Kz 557.4bn moved over Kwik in the first half of 2026, and that wallets were authorised to open e-money accounts about two years earlier.
Expansão reports EMIS data that wallets sent Kz 209.6bn to bank accounts and banks sent Kz 2.8bn to non-bank payment providers over Kwik in the first half of 2026.
Expansão reports Kwik, launched by the Banco Nacional de Angola in June 2023, carries instant transfers between banks and digital wallets, with Kz 557.4bn moved in the first half of 2026.
Angop reports Paypay's wallet processed 1,637,275 instant transfers in February 2026 through KWiK, with over 625 thousand active accounts, per EMIS's monthly report.
EMIS's report shows Paypay, BAI, Unitel Money's operator USPM and sixteen banks all transferring through the one KWiK instant-payment system in February 2026.
KWiK, reported by EMIS, handled 3.14 million transfers worth 74.6 billion kwanzas in February 2026 across wallets and banks, with 12.3 million registered accounts.
KWiK, the instant payment system developed by EMIS with Banco Nacional de Angola, processed 35 million transfers worth 590 billion kwanzas in 2025.
KWiK operates between all banks and payment service providers, enabling transfers between different banks and mobile wallets, with 22 institutions integrated.
KWiK connects banks and mobile wallets on one national instant payment system, per the CCENIF press note.
EMIS, Angola's interbank services company, manages the MULTICAIXA Express app and KWiK instant transfers, per an EMIS executive director at the 2026-10-12 CyberSecur Summit.
Minister Jose de Lima Massano said on 9 July 2026 that mobile and digital payments in Angola grew about 56% year on year by the end of the first half of 2026.

UNITEL Money, a mobile money service with agents and registered and active customers, operates in Angola, including informal markets in Luanda, Benguela, Huila, Huambo and Lunda-Norte, and IFC announced a 24-month advisory partnership with it.
BNA governor Manuel Tiago Dias said instant payments are expanding in Angola, notably Kwik, which allows real-time transfers, alongside QR code and contactless payments.
Africell Mobile Money entered operation as a payment service provider, with over 8.5 million registered accounts, and Unitel Money and PayPay also appear as non-bank providers.
Afrimoney, Unitelmoney and Paypay operate as non-bank digital money and payment platforms with customers filing complaints in Q2 2025.
